findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the echo-safety mechanism: inbound suppression is done by `RECONCILER_MARKER in body_text` in `inbound_collection_diffs.py`, NOT by `_is_machine_marker_comment` (which matches only BRIDGE_CANARY_ALERT/'Still stale as of' prefixes and never sees the marker because `_normalize_comment_body` strips it); update the Approach, Testing 'Echo-safe', and the marker-tagged AC to assert against the real inbound filter.
evidence: outbound_comments.py:375-382 `_is_machine_marker_comment` returns `normalized_body.startswith(_EXCLUDED_COMMENT_PREFIXES)` where prefixes are ('BRIDGE_CANARY_ALERT:', 'Still stale as of') — RECONCILER_MARKER is not among them
outbound_comments.py:206 `_normalize_comment_body` does `text.replace(RECONCILER_MARKER, '').strip()` — the marker is stripped before any machine-marker classification
inbound_collection_diffs.py:153-155 the real inbound echo filter: `body_text = _normalize_jira_body(...)` then `if RECONCILER_MARKER in body_text: continue # outbound echo`
inbound_fields.py:268-274 `_normalize_jira_body` preserves the marker precisely because 'callers filter on it'
findings.finding: The plan asserts echo-safety comes from _is_machine_marker_comment recognizing the RECONCILER_MARKer-tagged breadcrumb so inbound never echoes it back, but the code refutes this: _is_machine_marker_comment (outbound_comments.py:375-382) matches only _EXCLUDED_COMMENT_PREFIXES ('BRIDGE_CANARY_ALERT:', 'Still stale as of') and is an outbound exclusion, while inbound echo suppression is actually done by 'RECONCILER_MARKER in body_text' in inbound_collection_diffs.py:154. Additionally _normalize_comment_body strips RECONCILER_MARKER before classification, so the marker can never make _is_machine_marker_comment fire.
findings.location: Approach paragraph ('carry the RECONCILER_MARKER ... so _is_machine_marker_comment recognizes it and inbound never echoes it back'); Testing 'Echo-safe'; AC 'The breadcrumb is marker-tagged and not echoed inbound'
scenarios: Author wires the breadcrumb to rely on _is_machine_marker_comment for inbound suppression and it silently does nothing, letting the breadcrumb be re-ingested as user content
test_breadcrumb_echo_safe asserts against _is_machine_marker_comment classification and passes locally while the real inbound path (RECONCILER_MARKER in body_text) is what actually governs echo
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the echo-safe claim/test to assert the marker-tagged breadcrumb body is skipped by the inbound comment differ's `RECONCILER_MARKER in body_text` check in `inbound_collection_diffs.py` (line 154), and drop the reliance on `_is_machine_marker_comment` for inbound suppression.

findings.finding: The plan says the breadcrumb 'dedupe[s] on body so it appends exactly once ... reuses _diff_comments'. But _diff_comments dedupes a local comment against jira_bodies derived from the Jira snapshot/live client; the parent-divergence site has no snapshot/client, so the append-once guarantee has no described mechanism there.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the breadcrumb's behavior when the nearest-represented ancestor changes across passes (retire/supersede the stale comment or dedupe on a stable marker rather than exact body) and add a test for the ancestor-change case.
evidence: Plan: 'dedupe on body so it appends exactly once (idempotent across passes)' — body-keyed dedup is only idempotent while the computed ancestor/body is unchanged.
Plan: 'Walk ancestors upward to the nearest one that has a bound Jira key' — the nearest represented ancestor can change between passes as bindings/skip-sync state change, producing a different body.
ABSENCE: no retire/supersede path for a superseded breadcrumb is specified; the managed-comment machinery only appends and body-dedupes.
findings.finding: The breadcrumb dedupes on body and appends once, but the plan does not address staleness when the nearest-represented ancestor changes across passes: if a different ancestor becomes the nearest bound one (or an intervening skip-synced ancestor later syncs), the body-dedup keys on the OLD body, so a second breadcrumb naming the new key is appended while the stale breadcrumb persists — leaving conflicting parent hints and no retire/supersede path.
findings.location: Approach — 'dedupe on body so it appends exactly once (idempotent across passes)'
findings.suggested_fix: Dedupe/supersede on a stable per-child breadcrumb marker (e.g. the RECONCILER_MARKER plus a fixed breadcrumb tag) so a changed ancestor UPDATES the single breadcrumb rather than appending a second one, and note the retirement path when the parent becomes representable again.
